title: Basic probability

points.text: Trial, outcome, equally likely outcomes, relative frequency, sample space, event

bigPicture: Probability measures how likely an event is, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). With equally likely outcomes it is a matter of careful counting.

keyIdeas.answer: Trial: one performance of an experiment. Outcome: one possible result. Sample space U: all possible outcomes. Event: a set of outcomes. Relative frequency = number of times it happened ÷ number of trials; it estimates the probability.
P(A) = n(A)/n(U). The complement A′ (not A): P(A′) = 1 − P(A).
In n trials, expect n × P(A) occurrences. It need not be a whole number.

keyTerms.def: the set of all possible outcomes
observed proportion of trials in which an event happens

workedExamples.title: Two dice
workedExamples.prompt: Two fair dice are rolled. Find P(sum = 8).

misconceptions.wrong: The expected number must be a whole number
misconceptions.right: It is a long-run average, e.g. 2.5.
It estimates it; the estimate improves with more trials.

practice.prompt: A bag has 5 red, 3 blue and 2 green counters. One is drawn at random and replaced, 60 times. Find P(not red) and the expected number of greens.
A spinner lands on 4 in 37 out of 200 spins. Estimate P(4) and the expected number of 4s in 750 spins.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
